data.name: Ruthless Safari
data.detailed_description: The game's plot is straightforward and Ruthless Safari takes place in the desert where our heroine decided to take a picture of a lion on his head after the blinding flash, the furious animal rushes in pursuit of it, our task is to run and time to jump over obstacles such as cactus. Every encounter with cactus leaves our heroine without one set of clothes, and then leads to death. How long you will be able to avoid a terrible fate, depends on You!

reviews.review:
Ruthless Safari is a compact side-scrolling runner that builds its entire identity around a ridiculous safari trip gone disastrously wrong. Developed by SharkGame and published by Laush Studio, it favors immediate arcade action over complicated systems or a lengthy story. The premise is simple: a woman attempts to photograph a lion in the desert, the camera flash irritates the animal, and she suddenly finds herself running for her life. From there, the game becomes a test of timing, concentration, and how long the player can survive before an obstacle ends the escape.

The gameplay is intentionally straightforward. The character continuously moves forward, leaving the player primarily responsible for jumping over hazards scattered across the desert. Cacti represent one of the most important dangers, and the challenge comes from judging when to jump rather than controlling every aspect of movement. There is practically no learning curve, so a new player can understand the basic objective within moments. The downside is that this simplicity leaves little room for mechanical growth. Once the jumping rhythm has been learned, improvement mostly comes from sharpening reactions and becoming more consistent.

Failure is presented with an unusual sense of humor. Colliding with cacti can cause the heroine to progressively lose pieces of clothing before the run ultimately comes to an end. It is a deliberately provocative gimmick rather than a meaningful gameplay mechanic, but it gives the title some personality beyond its otherwise conventional endless-runner structure. Combined with the angry lion chasing the protagonist, the result is more absurd comedy than serious survival. Players who appreciate deliberately silly indie concepts may find the presentation amusing, while others may consider the gimmick fairly shallow.

The strongest part of the gameplay is the immediate retry appeal. A failed attempt does not require navigating complicated systems before trying again, making it easy to fall into the familiar pattern of telling yourself that the next run will be better. Distance becomes an informal measure of progress, while the included Steam achievements provide additional targets for players who enjoy completing small arcade games. Reaching those goals adds some purpose to repeated attempts, although they cannot completely compensate for the limited variety of the central mechanic.

Visually, the game keeps things simple enough that hazards remain easy to identify while moving. The desert environment suits the safari theme and avoids unnecessary visual clutter, which is useful in a game where a fraction of a second can determine whether a jump succeeds. However, environmental and mechanical repetition eventually becomes noticeable. There are not enough major changes to make long sessions feel substantially different from the opening attempts. Ruthless Safari therefore works considerably better as something played for short bursts than as a game intended to occupy an entire evening.

Its sound design and music similarly support the uncomplicated arcade presentation. The relatively gentle soundtrack creates a humorous contrast with the fact that the protagonist is desperately escaping a lion. Once players become comfortable with the timing, there can actually be a strangely relaxing quality to repeating runs and trying to push slightly farther. That relaxation disappears whenever an incorrectly timed jump abruptly ends a promising attempt, but the low complexity keeps frustration relatively manageable.

Technical demands are extremely modest, which suits a lightweight game of this kind. Ruthless Safari does not require powerful hardware or a large amount of storage, making it accessible to older computers. For Steam Deck users, there is no official Valve Steam Deck compatibility rating confirming the game as Verified or Playable, so its status should be considered Unknown or Unverified. Its simple control scheme and low hardware requirements suggest that it may be a reasonable candidate for handheld play, but that should not be confused with official compatibility certification, and individual configuration or compatibility issues may still occur.

The biggest limitation is longevity. There simply are not enough mechanics, environments, progression systems, or meaningful variations to keep the experience feeling fresh for very long. Its appeal depends heavily on whether the player enjoys score-chasing gameplay and repeated attempts at the same basic challenge. Someone looking for a substantial platformer, developed storyline, exploration, character progression, or deep arcade mechanics will find little of that here. The game instead embraces being a tiny, unusual distraction built around one joke and one easily understood gameplay loop.

Taken on those modest terms, Ruthless Safari has some charm. Its bizarre premise, uncomplicated controls, achievement goals, quick restarts, and undemanding technical requirements make it suitable for brief sessions. At the same time, the shallow mechanics and repetitive structure prevent it from developing into a particularly compelling runner. It delivers exactly the sort of strange indie novelty its concept promises, but once that novelty fades, there is not much underneath to sustain extended interest.

Rating: 5/10
